headline: 255 votes: Mirza Fakhrul elected as Bangladesh's 24th president
summary: The BNP candidate secured a decisive victory in the National Parliament, defeating opponent Oli Ahmed with 88 votes.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 24th President of Bangladesh, securing 255 votes in the National Parliament. His opponent, Oli Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, received 88 votes.

The election took place on Thursday, with 343 out of 349 members of parliament voting. Six MPs did not cast their votes, including independent MP Rumin Farhana and several BNP members who were abroad or receiving medical treatment.

Following the announcement of the results by Chief Election Commissioner A.M.M. Nasir Uddin, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the new president with a red rose. The event was marked by a spirit of bipartisanship, with Mirza Fakhrul embracing opposition leaders.
The presidency became vacant after President Mohammed Sahabuddin resigned on July 24 for health reasons. Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed had been serving as the acting president in the interim.
The Election Commission has issued a formal gazette notifying the election of Mirza Fakhrul. He is scheduled to take the oath of office on Friday evening.

International congratulations have already poured in from the United Kingdom and China, while domestic leaders including Professor Yunus and the Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer have also extended their greetings.

headline_marked: Traffic alerts: [[DMP issues directives for President's swearing-in]]
headline: Traffic alerts: DMP issues directives for President's swearing-in
summary: Special traffic restrictions will be in place around Bangabhaban on Friday from 3 PM to 9 PM to ensure smooth movement for guests.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has issued traffic directives for the swearing-in ceremony of the newly elected President, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, at Bangabhaban.
The ceremony is scheduled for Friday, August 21, at 7:30 PM. High-profile guests including the Prime Minister, Speaker, Chief Justice, and foreign diplomats will attend.
To ensure smooth movement for guests, special traffic restrictions will be apply from 3 PM to 9 PM on Friday in the Bangabhaban and surrounding areas.
Vehicles are prohibited from entering the Dilkusha commercial area (Bangabhaban Road) and RAJUK crossing (DIT Road) from the Aliko Gap of Motijheel Shapla Chattar.
Buses from Shapla Chattar and Dainik Bangla to RAJUK-Gulistan will be diverted via Dainik Bangla-UBL-Press Club or other alternative routes.

Commercial vehicles will be barred from moving from Dainik Bangla towards RAJUK. Vehicles from Hanif Flyover are advised to avoid U-turns at Zero Point and use alternative routes via Fulbaria or UBL crossing.
The DMP has requested drivers to avoid these roads and use alternative routes to minimize inconvenience. They have apologized for the temporary disruption in traffic flow.
caption:
Heads up, Dhaka drivers! Special traffic restrictions are coming to the Bangabhaban area this Friday.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has issued traffic directives for the swearing-in ceremony of the newly elected President, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, at Bangabhaban.

The ceremony is scheduled for Friday, August 21, at 7:30 PM. High-profile guests including the Prime Minister, Speaker, Chief Justice, and foreign diplomats will attend.

To ensure smooth movement for guests, special traffic restrictions will be apply from 3 PM to 9 PM on Friday in the Bangabhaban and surrounding areas.

Vehicles are prohibited from entering the Dilkusha commercial area (Bangabhaban Road) and RAJUK crossing (DIT Road) from the Aliko Gap of Motijheel Shapla Chattar.

Buses from Shapla Chattar and Dainik Bangla to RAJUK-Gulistan will be diverted via Dainik Bangla-UBL-Press Club or other alternative routes.

Commercial vehicles will be barred from moving from Dainik Bangla towards RAJUK. Vehicles from Hanif Flyover are advised to avoid U-turns at Zero Point and use alternative routes via Fulbaria or UBL crossing.

The DMP has requested drivers to avoid these roads and use alternative routes to minimize inconvenience. They have apologized for the temporary disruption in traffic flow.
